posts.caption: Big Red weighs just under nineteen hundred pounds, and she knows where every one of them is. The woman at the farm stand across the road waves at her every morning from forty feet away and has never once crossed it. Last month a delivery driver pulled in, spotted her over the gate, and sat in his truck for a full five minutes before getting out. She watched him the whole time with her glasses low on her nose. I signed for the package myself. He left without waiting for the receipt.
posts.first: When I first started boarding, a woman from the next farm told me she'd always wanted to ride but was too scared. Eight years later she still drives over every Sunday just to stand at the fence and look at the horses. She brings her own folding chair. We've never once talked about riding.

posts.caption: Pudding has been escaping the pony stall since July, and I've stopped being surprised about where he ends up. Tuesday it was the feed room. Last week it was the wash rack, standing under the hose like he'd paid for it. This morning I found him outside the tack room with a look I can only describe as rehearsed. I took the blankets back to the rack. He watched me hang every one. Then he went and stood by the door I had just closed. I'm ordering a better latch.
posts.first: My first pony learned to open every latch I owned by the time he was five. I switched to a carabiner. He took it off with his lips and dropped it in the water bucket. I think about that carabiner more than I'd like to admit. It's still down there.

posts.theme: the horse budget vs. the spouse
posts.quote: My husband asked what we'd do with an extra $900 a month. I said buy hay. He said besides hay. We sat in silence.
posts.first: I keep a spreadsheet for the barn expenses. Last winter my husband found it and read the whole thing in silence. At the bottom he asked where the line was for the pony's birthday cake. I told him it's under hay. He nodded and closed the laptop.

posts.caption: The hay guy comes every second Thursday at 6:40, in a truck that sounds like a coffee grinder. He has delivered to this barn since before I owned it. He unloads two hundred bales without saying a word, then stands at the end of the aisle and watches the old gray eat his first flake. Last week I finally told him the old guy likes the other stack better. He looked at me, looked at the horse, and said he'd known for years. He sets that first bale out anyway.
posts.first: My dad drove a feed truck for thirty-one years and never once let a customer carry their own bags. He'd say it was policy. It was not policy. He just liked watching the horses get their dinner before he left. He retired and still drives past the barn on Sundays.

posts.caption: We had a trail ride on the calendar for Saturday, and I had a thermos, a hat, and a sincere plan. The mare walked to the gate with me. She looked at the trail, looked at the sky, and turned around toward the barn without a word. I stood there holding a lead rope and my own good intentions. It was forty-one degrees. We spent the afternoon in her stall with a flake of hay and a clean blanket. I read two chapters. She slept through all of them, and the cat never moved.
posts.first: I used to feel guilty on the days we skipped our ride. Then my old trainer told me a horse has never once filed a complaint about a day off. I've kept that in my coat pocket for twelve years. It's gotten a lot of use.

posts.caption: My mare's supplement shelf has outgrown my own medicine cabinet. There are four tubs on it now, a scoop for each one, and a laminated chart on the feed room door that I made myself at eleven o'clock at night. She eats it all with her chin lifted like she's being served at a restaurant. Meanwhile I take my vitamins in the truck on the way to the barn, if I remember. The vet says she's in great shape for her age. I choose to believe the chart did that.
posts.first: The first time I put a supplement scoop in her grain she picked around it for two days like it was a personal insult. I switched to a sweeter one. She ate every flake and licked the bucket. She has never thanked me. I've never expected it.

Text at the top reads: I'm not getting older. I'm becoming a premium product with a supplement schedule.
